title: Availability tiers and depth of replacement — what official sources publish, measured

how_to_read.tier: OFFICIAL_* means the label was read off an official field. UNCLASSIFIED is never used.
how_to_read.depth_ordinal: Always blank. No official source publishes 1st/2nd/3rd string, so the ordinal is not available and is not invented.
how_to_read.depth_of_replacement: Measured as a change against a second official listing for the same club, and classified SAME 46 vs BELOW THE 46.
how_to_read.attribution: A change is attributed to injury only where the official report carries Out or Doubtful. Anything else stays blank.

capability_matrix.capability: Pregame depth chart with 1st/2nd/3rd string order
capability_matrix.observed: 404 — '404 - Flag on the Play.'; no chart, no player, no status
capability_matrix.consequence: A pregame '2nd-string' or '3rd-string' label cannot come from this route. Any such label in this repository would be invented, so none is published.

capability_matrix.observed: Roster table: name, jersey, position, status column reads ACT, height, weight, experience, college. No depth order, no starter flag.
capability_matrix.consequence: ACT proves a player is on the active roster. It is silent on who starts.

capability_matrix.capability: Injury report — practice participation and game status
capability_matrix.observed: Player, Position, Injuries, Practice Status, Game Status for 28 clubs. Week 11 report was not observable: /reg11 returned the Week 10 page.
capability_matrix.consequence: Answers 'who is ruled out or limited'. Never answers 'who takes his place'.

capability_matrix.capability: Official Game Book — starting lineups by slot, substitutions, DNP, inactives
capability_matrix.observed: Both clubs' offensive and defensive starting slots with jersey numbers, the full substitution list, Did Not Play and Not Active.
capability_matrix.answers_which_tier: starter vs dressed vs not dressed
capability_matrix.consequence: This is the ONLY official route that shows who actually started. It exists after the game. It gives no ordinal depth, so 'depth of replacement' must be measured as a change against a previous official listing, not read off a chart.

capability_matrix.capability: Game-day inactives as a pregame list
capability_matrix.observed: The NFL publishes an inactives article per slate; it appears close to kickoff and is a moving target. Not present for the Week 11 slate at capture time.
capability_matrix.answers_which_tier: available vs not available, 90 minutes out
capability_matrix.consequence: Useful for a live desk, not for a pre-week model. A snapshot is stale in hours.

irregularities.finding: In the Week 10 Game Book, the New York Giants offence column prints 'LB 52 A.Reese' as its eighth row, while the same player also appears in the defence column. A linebacker is not an offensive starter.
irregularities.evidence: '| RT | 72 J.Eluemunor | LB | 52 A.Reese |' then '| LB | 52 A.Reese | CB | 20 G.Newsome |' in the retrieved table for the Week 10 PDF.
irregularities.impact: The offence column may be missing one genuine starter, or the extraction may have duplicated a defence cell across the column boundary. Either way, the NYG offence listing has 12 rows where 11 are expected.
irregularities.disposition: The ambiguous row is excluded from slot comparison and from the tier table. The count is published as observed. Nothing is guessed to fill the gap.

irregularities.finding: The Week 5 Game Book lists the Washington Commanders' 2026 Week 5 starting centre as 63 L.Patrick; the Week 10 injury report lists Lucas Patrick with a concussion, Did Not Participate, Out.
irregularities.evidence: Week 5 book: 'C 63 L.Patrick'. Week 10 report: 'WAS|Lucas Patrick|C|Concussion|Did Not Participate In Practice|Out'.
irregularities.impact: This is the single cleanest example in the sample of a starter lost to a reported injury, and it is the case the tier method should catch.
irregularities.disposition: Recorded as an attributed change. 67 N.Allegretti started at centre in Week 10.

pregame_gaps.question: Which backups are behind which starters, before kickoff, for Week 11?
pregame_gaps.status: NOT KNOWABLE from any official source probed on 2026-11-14
pregame_gaps.what_exists: A post-game lineup (Game Book), a roster without order, and an injury report without depth.
pregame_gaps.what_would_make_it_knowable: An official pregame depth chart (currently 404) or an official pregame starting-lineup announcement. Neither was observed.
pregame_gaps.therefore: Every Week 11 pregame tier cell is blank in this repository, and the reason is recorded per row rather than filled with a guess.

pregame_gaps.question: Did a 2nd, 3rd or 4th string player replace a starter in Week 10?
pregame_gaps.what_exists: For WAS and NYG: yes, measured — see depth_changes below.
pregame_gaps.what_would_make_it_knowable: A Game Book per club per week. That exists for every completed game; it has simply not been transcribed for all of them.
pregame_gaps.therefore: The measurement method is proven on two clubs. Scaling it to 32 clubs is mechanical work, not a new idea, and is the highest-value next task.

summary.method_correction_included: row-by-row matching was rejected as unsound; see the METHOD NOTE in scripts/availability.py and IR-1
summary.what_this_proves: Depth of replacement IS measurable from official sources, but only retrospectively and only at the cost of transcribing a Game Book per club per week. It is NOT knowable before kickoff. That distinction is the answer to the requirement, and it is the same answer the repository gave before — now with a working method and two clubs of evidence behind it instead of an assertion.

next_task_to_scale.task: Transcribe the Week 11 Game Books for all 32 clubs and run this comparison against Week 10, producing a full depth-change table.
next_task_to_scale.cost: One PDF retrieval and ~60 transcribed lines per game, 16 games.
next_task_to_scale.why_it_matters: It would let the model test whether a below-the-46 replacement predicts a worse outcome than a same-46 replacement. That is a testable signal, which is more than any current strategy has.
next_task_to_scale.blocking: Nothing. It is available now and was not done here only because it is a separate, large transcription task.

caveats: Two clubs, two weeks. Nothing here generalises to the league on this sample.

A slot change can be caused by scheme, formation, or a coaching decision. The injury attribution is therefore one-directional: Out/Doubtful explains a change, but no flag does not prove there was no injury.
The Week 5 baseline is the prior meeting; a club's 46 changes across a season for reasons unrelated to injury, so BELOW THE 46 is a lower bound on depth, not a precise rank.
No Week 11 injury report was observable (probe P4), so no Week 11 pregame row exists.
